family: Conditional heteroskedastic lognormal with interpolated arithmetic means

assumptions.description: Transport the selected external aggregate patterns to the target without a target-outcome calibration offset. Geography, ancestry, cohort selection, treatment, fasting and assay differences remain unresolved; this is a scenario assumption, not validated transportability.

Treat source BMI-category HDL means as values at representative BMI anchors 17, 21.25, 25.5 and 30.5 kg/m^2. The two closed-bin anchors are midpoints; the open-bin anchors are assumed. Piecewise linear interpolation between anchors supplies a continuous model. For BMI below 17 use the underweight anchor.

Use a common additive age pattern across sex and BMI. Within each source BMI category assume the pooled age distribution also applies to each sex, so count-weighted category age contrasts can center sex-BMI means. This does not establish actual sex-specific source age distributions.

Convert reported SEM to SD as SEM*sqrt(n) under the conventional independent unweighted mean formula; use that broad-cell marginal SD as an approximate conditional variability scale rather than claiming it is a measured regression residual SD. This retains some variation due to unmodeled within-cell predictor variation.

Use a lognormal conditional distribution with exact arithmetic mean correction and source-derived coefficient of variation. Interpolate log variance across BMI anchors; hold CV constant with age and beyond extreme BMI anchors. This positive, right-skewed family and its tail behavior are not estimated from source quantiles.

Interpolate age contrasts at representative ages 35, 45, 55.5 and 65.5, hold the nearest value outside this knot range, and do not impose a menopausal discontinuity. Treat an adjusted source age contrast as a provisional age association in a model omitting other source covariates.

Beyond BMI 30.5, use longitudinal percent-change associations as provisional cross-sectional log-mean slopes: -0.0077 for men and -0.0042 for women per kg/m^2. This assumes local-percent-to-log approximation, extension across persons and transport across populations; it is a weak extrapolation choice, not an identified tail relationship.

Draw participants independently conditional on the three observed predictors using a local seed-controlled RNG; no unobserved family, household, race, lifestyle or clinical covariates are reconstructed. Draw-to-draw Monte Carlo variation does not represent epistemic parameter uncertainty.

bmi_knots.derivation: Midpoints of [18.5,24) and [24,27) are 21.25 and 25.5; 17 and 30.5 are assumed representatives of open-ended bins, not reported source means.

age_knots.derivation: Representative centers of printed age categories; boundary overlap is unresolved and no individual age distribution is inferred.

source_hdl_means.derivation: Exact printed Table 2 sex-BMI arithmetic means; age centering and interpolation described in equations.

source_cell_counts.derivation: Exact Table 2 counts; used only in SEM-to-SD conversion.

source_mean_standard_errors.derivation: Exact printed Table 2 SEMs, transformed to source SD=SEM*sqrt(n) then log variance=log(1+(SD/source_mean)^2).

source_age_counts_by_bmi.derivation: Exact Table 2 age counts; each row weights the corresponding age contrasts to center the sex-BMI mean anchor.

age_contrasts.derivation: Exact adjusted Table 3 contrasts, reference fixed to zero, used as additive mg/dL age function.

tail_log_slopes.derivation: Abstract percent changes -0.77 and -0.42 divided by 100, then used as approximate log-mean slopes above BMI 30.5.

equations: Let j index four BMI categories and s sex. c_j=sum_k(n_jk*a_k)/sum_k(n_jk).
HDL=exp(log(m)-v/2+sqrt(v)*Z), Z~N(0,1) independently, so E[HDL|x]=m and Var[HDL|x]=m^2*(exp(v)-1).
uncertainty: Fixed scenario parameters; stochastic residual draws only. Source uncertainty and transport uncertainty are not resolved by repeated draws.
alternatives_considered: Fully adjusted BMI contrasts: rejected as the sole BMI relationship because conditioning on TG, WHR and lifestyle changes the estimand.
Categorical step function: avoids midpoint assumptions but introduces discontinuities and zero within-category continuous BMI association.
Unbounded linear HDL mean: rejected for extreme BMI extrapolation because it can create nonpositive means.
Gaussian residuals with clipping: rejected because it introduces an arbitrary positive point mass; lognormal distribution is explicitly assumed.
Flat obesity tail: plausible sensitivity alternative, retained for checks because the selected longitudinal tail bridge is weak.
